Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to
address City Council, please complete a speaker card and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. City Council will hear public
comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote and on matters not listed on the agenda
during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for
consideration at a future City Council meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council: Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less
and
directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or
other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are
available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the
agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48
hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements
can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has
been posted will also be made available for public inspection. Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City
Clerk’s Department, during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every
other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

Gov. Code § 84308: Parties to any proceeding involving a license, permit, or other entitlement for use pending before the City
Council must disclose any campaign contribution over $500 (aggregated) within the preceding 12 months made by the party, their
agent, and those required to be aggregated with their contributions under Gov. Code § 82015.5. The disclosure must include the
amount contributed and the name(s) of the contributor(s). "G.C. § 84308: Yes" on this agenda indicates that the item is subject to
these regulations.

Mayor Ayala called the special State of the City meeting to order at 11:15 a.m. in the

absent. Also present were Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; and Christel Zamudio,

report on the Norwalk Chamber of Commerce. City Council received and filed.

the Norwalk Sheriff’s Station. City Council received and filed.

City Council received and filed.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

Councilmember Rios recognized October as Breast Cancer Awareness Month and
encouraged all to stay up to date on preventative care; highlighted the Paint the Town
Pink campaign in support of the American Cancer Society and invited all to attend the
Norwalk Chick-Fil-A fundraiser on October 22nd to support this worthy cause; reported
attending a youth event at Redeemer Covenant Church and the importance of providing
support to the youth in the community. Councilmember Valencia reported on her
attendance at the 40th Annual Arturo Sanchez Halloween Parade; thanked staff and the
Sanchez family for a great job; invited the community to visit the Norwalk Arts and Sports
Complex to view a collection of photos and memorabilia from the many Arturo Sanchez
Halloween Parades and to the City’s upcoming Halloween events. Vice Mayor Perez
reported on her attendance at the Annual League of California Cities conference held at
the Long Beach Convention Center; announced the City’s Teen Alliance Program was
awarded a Helen Putnam Award for Excellence; thanked staff and the community for a
wonderful Halloween Parade; commented on the California Contract Cities monthly
meeting and the “Women in Leadership” dinner meeting; congratulated staff and Mayor
Ayala on a wonderful State of the City; and wished everyone a Happy Halloween. Mayor
Ayala commented on the success of the Arturo Sanchez Halloween Parade and thanked
staff and the Sanchez family for a successful event; and shared that $15,000 dollars in
scholarships were awarded to bands that participated in the parade.

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

City Council recognized the American Cancer Society for their contributions.

City Council recognized the Southeast Area Animal Control Authority on their 50th
Anniversary.

RESOLUTION NO. 25-50 – APPROVING AN AMENDED AND RESTATED PARKING
AGREEMENT

Following a report by Alex Hamilton, Interim Director of Community Development,
Councilmember Ramirez moved and Councilmember Rios seconded to:
a. find that the Amended and Restated Parking Agreement is categorically exempt
  pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (“CEQA”) as this activity will not
  have a significant effect on the environment per Section 15301 Class 1 (Existing
  Facilities) of the CEQA Guidelines and CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3) –
  Common Sense Exemption in that it can be seen with certainty that there is no
  possibility that the Amended and Restated Parking Agreement may have a significant
  effect on the environment. None of the exceptions under CEQA Guidelines Section
  15300.2 apply;
b. adopt Resolution No. 25-50, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF NORWALK APPROVING AN AMENDED AND RESTATED PARKING

  “Title 15 BUILDINGS AND CONSTRUCTION

  Chapter 15.54 ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING STATIONS

15.54.010 Purpose

The purpose of this Chapter is to promote and encourage the use of electric vehicles by
creating an expedited, streamlined permitting process for electric vehicle charging
stations while promoting public health and safety and preventing specific adverse impacts
in the installation and use of such charging stations. This Chapter is also purposed to
comply with California Government Code Section 65850.7.

15.54.020 Definitions

  (a) “Electric vehicle charging station” or “charging station” means any level of electric
  vehicle supply equipment station that is designed and built in compliance with
  Article 625 of the California Electrical Code, as it reads on the effective date of this
  Chapter, and delivers electricity from a source outside an electric vehicle into a
  plug-in electric vehicle.

  (b) “Specific, adverse impact” means a significant, quantifiable, direct, and
  unavoidable impact, based on objective, identified, and written public health or
  safety standards, policies, or conditions as they existed on the date the application
  was deemed complete.

  (c) “Electronic submittal” means the utilization of one or more of the following:

  a. Electronic mail or email.
  b. The internet.
  c. Facsimile.

15.54.030 Expedited permitting process

Consistent with Government Code Section 65850.7, the Building Official shall implement
an expedited, streamlined permitting process for electric vehicle charging stations, and
adopt a checklist of all requirements with which electric vehicle charging stations shall
comply with in order to be eligible for expedited review. The expedited, streamlined
permitting process and checklist may refer to the recommendations contained in the most
current version of the “Plug-In Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Permitting Checklist” of the
“Zero-Emission Vehicles in California: Community Readiness Guidebook” as published
by the Governor’s Office of Planning and Research. The City’s adopted checklist shall
be published on the City’s website.

Ordinance No. 25-1760  Page 4 of 6
 15.54.040 Permit application processing

  (a) Prior to submitting an application for processing, the applicant shall verify that the
  installation of an electric vehicle charging station will not have specific, adverse
  impact to public health and safety and building occupants. Verification by the
  applicant includes but is not limited to: electrical system capacity and loads;
  electrical system wiring, bonding and overcurrent protection; building infrastructure
  affected by charging station equipment and associated conduits; areas of charging
  station equipment and vehicle parking.

  (b) A permit application that satisfies the information requirements in the City’s
  adopted checklist shall be deemed complete and be promptly processed. Upon
  confirmation by the Building Official that the permit application and supporting
  documents meets the requirements of the City adopted checklist, and is consistent
  with all applicable laws and health and safety standards, the Building Official shall,
  consistent with Government Code Section 65850.7, approve the application and
  issue all necessary permits. Such approval does not authorize an applicant to
  energize or utilize the electric vehicle charging station until approval is granted by
  the City. If the Building Official determines that the permit application is
  incomplete, he or she shall issue a written correction notice to the applicant,
  detailing all deficiencies in the application and any additional information required
  to be eligible for expedited permit issuance.

  (c) Consistent with Government Code Section 65850.7, the Building Official shall
  allow for electronic submittal of permit applications covered by this Ordinance and
  associated supporting documentations. In accepting such permit applications, the
  Building Official shall also accept electronic signatures on all forms, applications,
  and other documentation in lieu of a wet signature by any applicant.

15.54.050 Technical review

  (a) It is the intent of this Ordinance to encourage the installation of electric vehicle
  charging stations by removing obstacles to permitting for charging stations so long
  as the action does not supersede the Building Official’s authority to address higher
  priority life-safety situations. If the Building Official makes a finding based on
  substantial evidence that the electric vehicle charging station could have a specific
  adverse impact upon the public health or safety, as defined in this Chapter, the
  City may require the applicant to apply for a use permit.

  (b) In the technical review of a charging station, consistent with Government Code
  Section 65850.7, the Building Official shall not condition the approval for any
  electric vehicle charging station permit on the approval of such a system by an
  association, as that term is defined by Civil Code Section 4080.

Ordinance No. 25-1760  Page 5 of 6
 15.54.060 Electric vehicle charging station installation requirements

  (a) Electric vehicle charging station equipment shall meet the requirements of the
  California Electrical Code, the Society of Automotive Engineers, the National
  Electrical Manufacturers Association, and accredited testing laboratories such as
  Underwriters Laboratories, and rules of the Public Utilities Commission or a
  Municipal Electric Utility Company regarding safety and reliability.

  (b) Installation of electric vehicle charging stations and associated wiring, bonding,
  disconnecting means and overcurrent protective devices shall meet the
  requirements of Article 625 and all applicable provisions of the California Electrical
  Code.

  (c) Installation of electric vehicle charging stations shall be incorporated into the load
  calculations of all new or existing electrical services and shall meet the
  requirements of the California Electrical Code. Electric vehicle charging equipment
  shall be considered a continuous load.

  (d) Anchorage of either floor-mounted or wall-mounted electric vehicle charging
  stations shall meet the requirements of the California Building or Residential Code
  as applicable per occupancy, and the provisions of the manufacturer’s installation
  instructions. Mounting of charging stations shall not adversely affect building
  elements.”

SUBJECT: CONFIRM EMERGENCY WORK AT AQUATIC PAVILION

Background:

The Aquatic Pavilion pool experienced a pump and filtration system failure that rendered the
pool system inoperable. These critical components required immediate emergency action to
protect public health and safety and avoid prolonged facility closure. Waterline Technologies,
Inc., the City’s contractor for pool maintenance and chemical supplies for lap and wader pools
at the Aquatic Pavilion, was utilized for the aforementioned repairs. During this period, Public
Services staff drained the pool, scrubbed the interior walls, replaced main drain covers, and
refilled the pool water.

Repairs were completed during a four-week shutdown to restore the system to operational
status. The pool was rendered fully operational on September 12. The following work was
performed:

  •  Rebuild the pump using new seals and install the rotating assembly into the pump
  housing.
  •  Installed and bolted the pump housing and installed a new (Love-Joy) coupling connected
  to the motor.
  •  Removed two 8” gear-driven isolation valves and installed two new isolation valves.
  •  Dove the pool to remove plugs from the main drain, flood the pump, and confirm start-up
  with no leaks.
  •  Removed air from the filters, performed backwash cycles, and restored them to service.
  •  Installed influent manifolds in all three filters and secured plumbing with new stainless
  hardware.

  •  Installed and tightened man-way covers for all three filters.
  •  Restarted the main pump, ran backwash cycles, and confirmed heater functionality.
  •  Installed eight new main drain covers.

Annually, the City’s Engineering Division oversees its Capital Improvement Program which
encompasses over $100 million in infrastructure improvements. To support infrastructure
enhancements, the City relies on various restricted and grant funding sources to ensure the City
can fund these vital improvements.

To ensure the City can apply for, be awarded with, and oversee the management of these
various restricted and grant funding sources, staff has identified the need for grant management
services. These services will supplement the work staff is doing to secure public infrastructure
improvements, seek new funding sources, and manage the post-award compliance
requirements set forth by various granting agencies.

On June 3, 2025, the City released Request for Proposal (“RFP”) No. 25-818 to solicit proposals
for On-Call Grant Management Services with the intent to develop a shortlist of qualified firms.
Services requested included grant research efforts, grant writing/applications, and post-award
compliance. A total of 16 proposals were received and scored by an evaluation committee
comprised of City staff based on the criteria set forth in the RFP document..

SUBJECT: ADVISORY BODY APPOINTMENTS

Background:

With the exception of the Planning Commission (which is commensurate with the appointing
Councilmember’s term) and five members of the Art in Public Places Commission (which is
established in the Norwalk Municipal Code), Advisory Body terms are for two years following a
City election. Advisory Body terms are from January 1, of odd years to December 31, of even
years.

There are vacancies on several Advisory Bodies: Art in Public Places (3), Historical Heritage (6),
International Friendship (1), Public Safety (4), Senior Citizens (1), and the Youth Commission
(14). The Youth Commission has one member at this time. The age range for the Youth
Commission is between 13 to 18 years of age. Each City Councilmember has three
appointments.

Two of the vacancies on the Art in Public Places Committee are appointed based on Norwalk
Municipal Code §15.44.060, and require consensus of the entire City Council. Any
Councilmember may nominate an individual who falls into one of the two categories:
Business/Community College Representative and at-large Community Representative.

Fiscal Impact:

N/A

Citizens Advised:

Citizens are notified of Advisory Body vacancies through posting of vacancy notices and the
Advisory Body term list, both of which are posted on the City’s website and at City Hall.

SUBJECT: ORDINANCE NO. 25-1761 – ADOPTING THE 2025 CALIFORNIA BUILDING,
  RESIDENTIAL, FIRE, WILDLAND-URBAN INTERFACE, PLUMBING,
  ELECTRICAL, MECHANICAL, ENERGY, EXISTING BUILDING, AND GREEN
  BUILDING STANDARDS AND AMENDMENTS AND AMENDING THE
  NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE

Background:

The California Building Standards Commission (CBSC) is responsible for adopting and
publishing the building codes used for construction within the state. The International Building
Code, published approximately every three years by the International Code Council (ICC),
serves as the model code referenced by California. The CBSC makes state-specific
amendments to the International Building Code and publishes the California Building Standards
Code, Title 24 of the California Code of Regulations.

Building and Safety activities are regulated and controlled very closely by State Law and local
ordinances. The CBSC adopted and published the 2025 edition of the California Code of
Regulations Title 24, otherwise known as the 2025 California Codes. As mandated by state law,
cities must enforce these codes for all construction after January 1, 2026.

The California Codes are applicable to all occupancies throughout the state, whether or not the
local government takes an affirmative action to adopt these standards. California law takes a
straightforward approach to amendments by local governments:

  •  The governing body of the local government must make express findings that
  amendments to the building standards are necessary due to local climatic, topographic
  or geologic conditions. The local amendments may only provide for a more restrictive
  building standard than that contained in the California Codes.
 City Council  November 4, 2025

  •  The administrative provisions of the California Codes may also be amended, provided
  they are found to be equivalent to the provisions outlined in the Codes.
  •  The local amendments and the express findings must be filed with the California Building
  Standards Commission.

In accordance with these requirements, staff has identified the climatic, geologic, and
topographic conditions within the City’s region that necessitate amendments to the California
Codes. These findings include the hot dry Santa Ana wind conditions, the occasional heavy
winter rains that follow the dry seasonal weather, the City’s location within a highly active seismic
area, the soils potential for liquefaction, the density of development, and existing traffic circulation
and congestion.

Most of the changes and modifications are the same or substantially similar to those that the City
has adopted for previous codes. The modifications to the California Codes contain vital
provisions regarding administrative procedures, roofing materials, seismic requirements,
foundation requirements, pool safety barriers and other matters necessitated by the City’s
exposure to the above climatic, geologic, and topographic conditions.

Some of the significant changes to the 2025 California Building Standards Codes:

California Building Code:
  • Automatic sprinkler systems are required to be installed in Group B, F-1, M and S-1
  occupancies that have lithium-ion or lithium-metal battery systems.
  • Guards required on retaining walls.
  • Public-occupancy temporary structures added which allows for up to one year of
  installation.

California Residential Code:
  • Building Integrated Photovoltaic system (BIPV) criteria has been added.
  • The thickness of required under slab vapor retarders has returned to 6 mil.

California Wildland-Urban Interface Code:
  • Introduces Part 7: the California Wildland-Urban Interface Code.

This new part integrates California Residential Code section R337, California Building Code
chapter 7A, and California Fire Code Chapter 49 to strengthen wildfire resilience in areas where
development meets wildland.

California Energy Code:
  • Updates mandatory U-factor 0.40 for fenestration in all climate zones.
  • Updates mandatory BESS-ready applies to newly constructed single-family buildings with
  dwelling unit electrical service over 125A.
  • Requires electric readiness for newly constructed commercial kitchens.
  • Expanded PV Solar and battery requirements to certain occupancy types.

Adoption Process:
Government Code §50022.1, et seq., authorizes the adoption by reference of the codes specified
in this ordinance. When adopting a code by reference, State law requires that the City Council
schedule a Public Hearing after first reading of the ordinance. The Public Hearing can occur in
conjunction with the second reading of the ordinance. Pursuant to Government Code Section
50022.3, the notice of the Public Hearing must be published once a week for two successive
weeks, with at least five days intervening between the respective publication dates.

Copies of the California Building Codes have been deposited with the City Clerk for public review
until adoption and shall be kept in the Building & Safety office after the adoption pursuant to
Government Code §50022.6.

Environmental Review:
The California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) does not apply to continuing administrative
activities or organizational activities of government that will not result in specific direct or indirect
physical changes in the environment, or to the creation of government funding mechanisms or
other governmental fiscal activities that do not result in potential environmental impacts. Public
Resources Code Section 21065 and State CEQA Guidelines Sections 15378(b)(2) and
(b)(5). The draft ordinance makes various technical changes to the existing regulations in the
form of local administrative, climate, geologic or topographical changes. On that basis, the draft
ordinance is not subject to CEQA.

Fiscal Impact:

Training costs and the purchase of new code books for Building & Safety staff is included in FY
2025/26 budget.

Notice of the Public Hearing posted on October 31, 2025.

SUBJECT: RESOLUTION NO. 25-52 – APPROVING THE SECOND AMENDMENT TO THE
  GROUND LEASE, AN EASEMENT AGREEMENT, AND COVENANTS,
  CONDITIONS, AND RESTRICTIONS FOR THE WALK PROJECT SITE

Background:

The Ground Lease Agreement between the City and Primestor Norwalk Entertainment. LLC
(“Primestor”) was approved in October 2022 (“Original Ground Lease”). The City leased a
portion of City Property, including but not limited to the Surface Parking Area, to Primestor for
the development and construction of a mixed use development (the “Project”) consisting of (i)
approximately three hundred seventy-four (374) residential units; (ii) approximately 94,398
square feet of commercial uses, which may include, but not be limited to, food and beverage
establishments, retail, health and wellness facilities, and grocery or supermarket uses; and (iii)
approximately 119,643 square feet of ground-floor open space/plaza area that is publicly
accessible but privately maintained and operated. The City Council subsequently approved the
First Amendment to the Ground Lease in January 2025.

Analysis:

A.  Second Amendment to Ground Lease (“Second Amendment”)

The Second Amendment proposes to amend the Original Ground Lease in order to: (i)
acknowledge and confirm that the Affordable Housing Parcel has been released from the
Premises under the Ground Lease. Under the terms of the Original Ground Lease, it was
anticipated that portions of the Project would be released from the Original Ground Lease to
facilitate the financing and development of individual components of the Project. Following the
said release, the Affordable Housing Parcel will be subject to an affordable housing ground
lease; (ii) increase the area of the Premises under the Original Ground Lease to include the area
adjacent to the City Hall building; and (iii) apply a rent credit against first and second year rent
 City Council  November 4, 2025

Conditions and Restrictions

payments consistent with the terms of the Exclusive Negotiation Agreement previously entered
into by and between the City and Primestor (“ENA”).

In addition, the Second Amendment also adds property adjacent to the City Hall building
measuring approximately 5,615 square feet to the Premises under the Original Ground Lease
which will be improved and incorporated into the Project’s community serving plaza.

Lastly, the Second Amendment also amends the Original Ground Lease to provide for the
reimbursement of certain Project entitlement costs incurred by Primestor in accordance with the
terms of the ENA as a credit against the first and second year rent. Under the Second
Amendment, Primestor would be entitled to a rent credit of $500,000 in year 1 and $397,747.25
rent credit in year 2 for Project entitlement costs.

B.  Easement Agreement

The City and Primestor desire to enter into an Easement Agreement in order to grant certain
non-exclusive rights in, on, over, under, across, and through the easement area on the City Hall
Parcel (as shown below) to Primestor to develop and construct improvements within the
easement area that will be seamlessly integrated with the Project’s community plaza. After
completion, Primestor will be responsible for ongoing maintenance of the easement area
improvements.

C.  Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions (“CC&R”)

Also for City Council’s consideration is the Declaration of CC&Rs for the common areas within
the Project that will be shared by the City and the Project’s commercial and residential

components such as the community plaza, all sidewalks, driveways, landscape and other
improvements (excluding buildings).

The CC&R is a legal document establishing a set of legal rules and terms that govern how the
Project common areas will be used and maintained and the duties and obligations of the
parties. The CC&R ensures that the Project common areas are managed and well maintained
for the life of the Project. CC&Rs are very common tools for all master planned development
types from residential condominiums, office, retail, and industrial developments that have single
or multiple common ownership interests in the project.

The CC&R is set up to allow for Primestor to assume the responsibilities for all maintenance
obligations and then offset set costs as part of the “operating expenses”. The final amount of
offset will be subject to City and Primestor annual review of expenses that would be applied
against base rent paid to the City by Primestor.

Environmental:

The City Council certified the Final Environmental Impact Report for the Project on October 4,
2022 through City Council Resolution No. 22-57 (“FEIR”), which evaluated the environmental
impacts associated with development and implementation of the Project. The Second
Amendment to the Ground Lease, Easement Agreement, and the CC&R are actions associated
with the implementation of the Project and are within the scope of the FEIR and none of the
conditions set forth under California Environmental Quality Act (“CEQA”) Guidelines Section
15162 requiring the preparation of a subsequent EIR have been met. Therefore, pursuant to
CEQA Guidelines Sections 15162 and 15168(c)(2), no further environmental review is required.

Fiscal Impact:

The City will receive sales taxes, property taxes, and percentage rent payments from the Mixed-
Use Project. All revenue receipts including net percentage rent payments will be subject to
annual review and approval of a financial statement submitted every calendar year pursuant to
the terms of the Ground Lease.

Tenant of its decision to lease a portion of the City Hall Parcel measuring approximately 5,615
square feet , as depicted on Exhibit A (the “City Hall Adjacent Area”), and Tenant has notified
City of its election to lease a portion of the City Hall Parcel from City, on the terms and
conditions set forth in the Ground Lease;

  WHEREAS, the City also desires to grant to Developer certain non-exclusive
easement rights in, on, over, under, across, and through the City Hall Parcel, but excluding
 the City Hall Building itself to develop certain improvements on the City Hall Parcel and to
provide for certain maintenance obligations and responsibilities, as depicted in Exhibit B (“City
Hall Parcel Easement”);

  WHEREAS, pursuant to Section 4 of the ENA (as defined in the Original Ground
Lease), Tenant has submitted Entitlement Cost Invoices to City evidencing Entitlement Costs
incurred by Primestor Development, Inc., a Nevada corporation, an affiliate of Developer and
City desires to reimburse Developer a portion of the Entitlement Cost Invoices consistent with
the ENA as by applying a credit against Developer’s obligation to pay Base Rent for the First
Rent Year and Second Rent Year;

  WHEREAS, the Developer desires to utilize State Density Bonus Law, which allows
developers to build more housing units than normally permitted by local zoning laws if they
include a certain percentage of affordable housing units within their development; and

  WHEREAS, the Parties now desire to amend the Original Ground Lease in order to:
(i) acknowledge and confirm that the Affordable Housing Parcel has been released from the
Premises under the Ground Lease; (ii) increase the area of the Premises under the Ground
Lease to include the City Hall Adjacent Area; (iii) apply the Rent Credit against Base Rent for
the First Rent Year and Second Rent Year; and (iv) make such other modifications and
amendments to the Original Ground Lease.

  NOW, THEREFORE, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK HEREBY
DETERMINES, FINDS, AND RESOLVES AS FOLLOWS:

  Section 1. The foregoing recitals are true and correct and are hereby incorporated
as substantive findings in this Resolution.

  Section 2. The City Council certified the Final EIR for the Project on October 4,
2022, through City Council Resolution No. 22-57 (“FEIR”), which evaluated the environmental
impacts associated with development and implementation of the Project. The Second
Amendment to the Ground Lease, Easement Agreement, and the CC&R are actions
associated with the implementation of the Project and are within the scope of the FEIR and
none of the conditions set forth under CEQA Guidelines Section 15162 requiring the
preparation of a subsequent EIR have been met. Therefore, pursuant to CEQA Guidelines
Sections 15162 and 15168(c)(2), no further environmental review is required.

  Section 3. The City Council hereby finds that the Second Amendment to the Ground
Lease, Easement Agreement, and the CC&R are consistent the overall policies, goals, and
objectives of the City’s General Plan, adopted specific plans, and the Norwalk Municipal Code
based on the facts and findings set forth City Council Resolution No. 22-58, which are
incorporated and made a part of herein. In addition, the Second Amendment to the Ground
Lease, Easement Agreement, and the CC&R are consistent with the goals and policies of the
City’s Housing Element by facilitating: (1) the development of market-rate and affordable
housing supply to meet the needs projected for the City; (2) provide a variety of housing
opportunities for all income groups of the City; (3) attain a housing market where all families
can find adequate housing within their financial means; and (4) achieve an assisted
housing supply that provides a full range of affordable ownership and rental housing
opportunities.

   Section 4. The City Council further finds Second Amendment to the Ground Lease,
Easement Agreement, and the CC&R assist in maximizing local economic development and
housing goals as follows: (i) creation of local, well-paid, and skilled and trained construction
jobs at prevailing rates in connection with the Residential and Commercial Projects, (ii)
creation of well-paid new commercial retail jobs once the Project is completed; (iii) the
generation of new property and sales tax revenue and lease rent that may be used to provide
vital City services for the residents of the City, businesses and their employees, and visitors
to the City, (iv) generate provide new amenities for the residents of the City and serve as a
regional commercial destination in the southeast Los Angeles County area as well as an
economic node and priority opportunity site, (v) assist meeting the City’s regional housing
goals through the construction of the residential units consisting of affordable and market rate
units, and (vi) creation of improved, publicly accessible open space for gatherings.

  Section 5. The City Council hereby approves (i) Second Amendment to the Ground
Lease, (ii) the Easement Agreement, and (iii) the CC&R. The City Manager or designee are
hereby authorized and directed to execute Second Amendment to the Ground Lease,

effectuate the intent of the any of the approved agreements set forth under this Resolution

  Section 6. The City Council further authorizes the City Manager or his designee

  Section 7. The City Clerk shall certify the adoption of this Resolution and it shall go
into effect immediately upon its adoption.

  Section 8. The Mayor, or presiding officer, is hereby authorized to affix his signature

  EASEMENT AGREEMENT

referred to herein as a “Party” and collectively, as the “Parties.”

  RECITALS

  A.  City is the fee owner of certain real property located in the City of Norwalk, County
of Los Angeles, State of California, more particularly described on Exhibit A (the “City
Property”).

  B.  A certain portion of the City Property, as more particularly described on Exhibit B-
1 and depicted on Exhibit B-2 (the “City Hall Parcel”), is currently improved with that certain
building located at 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California (the “City Hall Building”).

  C.  Pursuant to that certain Ground Lease by and between City and Developer dated
December 19, 2022 (the “Original Ground Lease”), as amended by that certain First Amendment
to Ground Lease dated March 31, 2025 (the “First Amendment”) and by that certain Second
Amendment to Ground Lease dated ______ (the “Second Amendment,” and collectively with the
Original Ground Lease, and the First Amendment, the “Ground Lease”), City leases to Developer,
and Developer leases from City, a portion of the City Property, as more particularly described on
Exhibit C (the “Premises”). The Premises do not include the City Hall Parcel.

  D.  In accordance with the Ground Lease, Developer intends to construct, operate and
maintain a mixed-use development (the “Project”) on the City Property. The Project will include
certain improvements on the City Hall Parcel (the “Easement Plaza Improvements”).

  E.  Pursuant to that certain Restricted Residential Ground Lease dated
_____________, by and between City and Residences at the Walk LP, a California limited
partnership (“Affordable Housing Developer”), an affiliate of Developer, City leases to

  -1-
 Affordable Housing Developer, and Affordable Housing Developer leases from City, a portion of
the City Property, as more particularly described on Exhibit D (the “Affordable Housing
Premises”), for the construction, operation and maintenance of a multifamily residential
development (the “Affordable Housing Project”).

  F.  The Parties desire to enter into this Agreement in order to provide Developer with
rights in, on, over, under, across, and through an area of the City Hall Parcel, as more particularly
described on Exhibit E (the “Easement Area”), in order to develop the Easement Plaza
Improvements, and to provide for certain maintenance obligations and allocate certain
responsibilities with respect thereto.

  AGREEMENT

incorporated into this Agreement as if set forth in full herein, mutual covenants, promises and
undertakings contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and
adequacy of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties hereby as follows:

benefit of Developer and its Permittees, an irrevocable, perpetual, non-exclusive easement (the
“Easement”)  in, on, over, under,
and across the Easement Area to construct, maintain, repair, operate, replace, reconstruct, relocate,
remove, use, and occupy the Easement Plaza Improvements and all incidental uses related thereto.

Developer, and any successor owner of the Affordable Housing Project, and their employees,
agents, representatives, contractors, subcontractors, consultants, customers, family, guests,
invitees, tenants, licensees, and concessionaires a non-exclusive easement, license, or other similar
right, in, on, over, across, and through the Easement Area for purposes of accessing and using the
Easement Plaza Improvements.

  1.2  No Public Dedications. No easement or other right granted in this
Agreement is intended to, nor shall it, constitute a dedication to the public of any property on the
City Hall Parcel or create any public right-of-way thereon, unless specifically provided for in this

  THIS DECLARATION OF COVENANTS, CONDITIONS AND RESTRICTIONS AND
ESTABLISHMENT OF EASEMENTS FOR NORWALK ENTERTAINMENT DISTRICT MIXED-
USE DEVELOPMENT (PLAZA) (this “Declaration”) is made as of the ___ day of ________, 2025
by PRIMESTOR NORWALK ENTERTAINMENT LLC, a Delaware limited liability company
(“Master Project Owner”), RESIDENCES AT THE WALK LP, a California limited partnership
(“Affordable Housing Project Owner”), and collectively with the Master Project Owner, the
“Owners”), THE CITY OF NORWALK, a California municipal corporation (the “City”), with
reference to the facts set forth below. Each of the Owners and the City are occasionally referred
to herein as the “Parties” and individually as a “Party.”

  RECITALS

  All initially capitalized terms used but not defined in the Recitals shall have the meanings
set forth in Article 1.

  A.  The City is the owner of certain real property located in the City of Norwalk, County
of Los Angeles, State of California, more particularly described on Exhibit A, (the “City Property”),
a portion of which is currently improved with the City’s City Hall building.

  B.  The City and Master Project Owner are parties to that certain Ground Lease dated
December 19, 2022 (the “Original Agreement”), as amended by that certain First Amendment
to Ground Lease dated March 19, 2025 (the “First Amendment” and together with the Original
Agreement, the “Original Ground Lease”), and by that certain Second Amendment to Ground
Lease dated _____, 2025 (the “Second Amendment” and together with the Original Ground
Lease, the “Ground Lease”). Pursuant to the Original Ground Lease, the City ground leased to
the Master Project Owner a portion of the City Property (the “Original Premises”), for the
development of a mixed-use development (the “Original Project”) consisting of (i) approximately
three hundred seventy-four (374) residential units; (ii) approximately ninety-four thousand three
hundred ninety-eight (94,398) square feet of commercial uses, which may include, but not be
limited to, food and beverage establishments, retail, health and wellness facilities, and grocery or
supermarket uses; and (iii) approximately one hundred nineteen thousand six hundred forty-three
(119,643) square feet of ground-floor open space/plaza area that is publicly accessible but
privately maintained and operated. Portions of the Original Project are to be constructed on
portions of the City Property that are outside of the Original Premises.

  C.  Pursuant to that certain [Assignment and Assumption of Ground Lease dated
______], and in accordance with Section 2.6 of the Original Ground Lease, Master Project Owner
assigned to Affordable Housing Project Owner all of Master Project Owner’s rights, title, and
interest in, to and under the Original Ground Lease with respect to the portion of the Original
Premises identified as Parcel 7 (the “Affordable Housing Premises”) with an affordable housing
project (the “Affordable Housing Project” and together with the Master Project, the “Project”)
consisting of fifty-six (56) residential units, including not less than fifty-three (53) income restricted
residential units and one (1) manager’s unit. The term “Master Project” shall refer to the Original
Project less the improvements that constitute the Affordable Housing Project.

240579601.16
238437-10002
   D.  Pursuant to that certain [Restricted Residential Ground Lease dated _______], by
and between Affordable Housing Project Owner and the City (the “Affordable Housing Ground
Lease”), the City ground leased the Affordable Housing Premises to the Affordable Housing
Project Owner for the development of the Affordable Housing Project.

  E.  Pursuant to the Second Amendment, the City and Master Project Owner confirmed
that, upon execution of the Affordable Housing Ground Lease, the Affordable Housing Premises
were released from the Original Premises and that the Original Premises were expanded to
include an additional portion of the City Property, such that the ground leased premises include
Parcels 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, and 10, as more particularly described in the Second Amendment (the
“Ground Lease Premises”).

  F.  As part of the Master Project, the Master Project Owner will develop a portion of
the Ground Lease Premises, as depicted on Exhibit C attached hereto (the “Ground Lease Plaza
Improvements Area”), with a plaza, sidewalks, driveways, landscaping, and other improvements
from time to time (the “Ground Lease Plaza Improvements”), including but not limited to a paseo
in the area depicted on Exhibit C (the “Paseo”), but excluding all Buildings (defined below) thereon
and all improvements located within any Building; provided, however, Ground Lease Plaza
Improvements shall not include improvements within the Ground Lease Premises dedicated for
Master Project Owner’s exclusive and/or dedicated use consistent with the Specific Plan and
other associated City approvals.

  G.  Pursuant to that certain Easement Agreement dated _______2025, by and
between Master Project Owner and the City (the “Easement Agreement”), the City has provided
Master Project Owner with an irrevocable, perpetual, non-exclusive easement
  in, on, over, and across a portion of
the City Property, as more particularly identified on Exhibit B (the “City Easement Area”) for the
development, construction, use, operation, and maintenance of certain parking and plaza
improvements for the Master Project (collectively, the “Easement Plaza Improvements”),
including but not limited to a surface parking lot in the area depicted in Exhibit C (the “Retail
Parking Area”), sidewalks, driveways, landscaping, and other improvements from time to time.
The Ground Lease Plaza Improvements together with the Easement Plaza Improvements shall
be referred to herein as the “Plaza Improvements.” The City Easement Area together with the
Ground Lease Plaza Improvement Area shall be referred to herein as the “Plaza Improvements
Area.”

  H.  This Declaration establishes easements for the benefit of the Ground Lease
Premises and the Affordable Housing Premises subject to the covenants, restrictions,
reservations, and limitations contained herein. This Declaration shall be liberally construed to
effectuate its purpose of creating a flexible plan for the maintenance, operation and governance
of the Plaza Improvements Area. To achieve these goals and to ensure a flexible governance
structure, further rights, obligations, allocations, easements and other matters affecting the Plaza
Improvements Area may be identified in Supplementary Declarations recorded in the future.

  DECLARATION

  NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the foregoing Recitals, which are hereby
incorporated into this Declaration as if set forth in full herein, and for other good and valuable
consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, each of the
Declarants declare that their respective interests in the City Property, as applicable, shall be, held,
conveyed, hypothecated, encumbered, leased, rented, used and occupied subject to the following

  ARTICLE 7

  7.1  Purpose of Assessments. The Assessments levied by the Common Area
Manager shall be used to perform the obligations and duties of the Common Area Manager under
this Declaration and for such other purposes as provided for in this Declaration.

  7.2  Annual Operating Budget and Assessment Commencement Date.

  7.2.1  No later than October 1st of each calendar year, commencing within the
year of achievement of substantial completion, the Common Area Manager shall submit to the
Parties a detailed proposed Annual Operating Budget for the upcoming calendar year. Each
Annual Operating Budget shall be prepared in accordance with the provisions of this Declaration
and Applicable Laws. Each Party hereby acknowledges and agrees that is has received a
preliminary draft of the initial Annual Operating Budget, and further agrees that such initial draft
is subject to revision and further subject to approval by the Parties in accordance with the
applicable terms and conditions of this Declaration. Each Party shall have the right, within thirty
(30) days following receipt of a proposed Annual Operating Budget, to review the same and
provide written notice to the Common Area Manager of its approval or its disapproval, provided
that any disapproval notice (a “Budget Disapproval Notice”) shall set forth in reasonable detail
the reasons for such disapproval and the changes required for approval, and provided further that
no approval shall be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. If a Party properly delivers
a Budget Disapproval Notice, then within ten (10) business days after receipt of the Budget
Disapproval Notice the Common Area Manager shall address the reasons for disapproval set
forth in the Budget Disapproval Notice and provide a revised proposed Annual Operating Budget
to all Parties. Each Party shall have ten (10) business days from receipt of the revised proposed
Annual Operating Budget to respond by written notice in the same manner as provided above
with respect to the original proposed Annual Operating Budget. All Parties and the Common Area
Manager shall mutually cooperate in good faith to promptly resolve any disapproved items in a
proposed Annual Operating Budget and generate an Annual Operating Budget reasonably
acceptable to all Parties. Time is of the essence with respect to the delivery of any Budget
Disapproval Notice and any subsequent objections, and any failure to properly object in writing in
accordance with the provisions above shall be deemed approval by a Party. If for any reason the
Parties have not all agreed upon (or be deemed to have agreed upon) a new Annual Operating
Budget prior to the beginning of the new calendar year, the approved Annual Operating Budget
for the prior year, plus an increase equal to the percentage increase (but not decrease) in the
local Consumer Price Index during the prior year (the ”CPI Increase”), shall be used until the new
Annual Operating Budget is approved pursuant to this paragraph. Upon approval of the new
Annual Operating Budget by all Parties, Assessments shall be retroactive to the first day of the
Fiscal Year. If the amount paid utilizing the approved Annual Operating Budget for the prior year
(plus any CPI Increase) exceeds the new Annual Operating Budget, the Common Area Manager
shall apply such excess amounts against Assessments to be levied as of the date of the new
Annual Operating Budget approval and for the following months until the excess amounts are
applied in full. If the amount paid utilizing the approved Annual Operating Budget for the prior
year (plus any CPI Increase) shall be less than the new Annual Operating Budget, the Parties
shall pay the balance of such deficiency within thirty (30) days after the date of the new Annual
Operating Budget approval. If the Parties are unable, despite good faith and commercially
reasonable efforts, to agree upon an Annual Operating Budget by March 31st of any calendar
year, it shall be an Operational Dispute (defined below) subject to arbitration under Section 14.3.

   7.10  Reconciliation and Audit Rights.

  7.10.1  Reconciliation. Within ninety (90) days after the end of each Fiscal Year,
or portion thereof the Common Area Manager shall provide each Party with a statement setting
forth the actual Common Expenses paid by the Common Area Manager for the operation and
maintenance of the Plaza and performance of its other obligations hereunder and such Party’s
applicable Allocable Share (such statement and supporting data are collectively called the
“Reconciliation”). The Reconciliation shall separately identify cost categories for the various
Common Expenses and the applicable Allocable Shares. If the amount paid by a Party for such
Fiscal Year shall have exceeded the expenses incurred by the Common Area Manager for the
applicable Allocable Shares (“Actual Expenses”), the Common Area Manager may refund the
excess to the Parties at the time the Reconciliation is delivered or apply such amounts against
Assessments to be levied for the next Fiscal Year. If the amount paid for such Fiscal Year shall
be less than the Actual Expenses, the Party shall pay the balance of such Party’s Allocable Share
to the Common Area Manager within sixty (60) days after receipt of such Reconciliation, it being
understood and agreed that the sixty (60) day period only establishes the period for payment and
is not to be construed as an acceptance of the Reconciliation.

  7.10.2  Audit Rights. Within two (2) years after the date of receipt of a
Reconciliation, the Parties shall each have the right to audit the books and records pertaining to
the Common Expenses for the Fiscal Year covered by such Reconciliation. In connection
therewith, the Common Area Manager shall cause to be maintained at its offices or at the Los
Angeles County offices of any Management Company it engages to perform its services
hereunder, all books and records pertaining to the operation and maintenance of the Plaza
Improvements Area. Such Parties shall notify the Common Area Manager of their intent to audit
at least fifteen (15) business days prior to the designated audit date. Any such audit shall be
provided to the Common Area Manager upon completion. In the event that such audit shall
disclose any error in the determination of the Common Expenses, or the allocation thereof to a
Party, leading to an overestimate or underestimate of the Assessment of any Party, then an
appropriate adjustment shall be made forthwith. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, the
approval of a prior Reconciliation, or any line item comprising a part thereof, shall not be a waiver
of a Party’s right to challenge subsequent Reconciliations regarding such line item. The cost of
any audit shall be assumed by the auditing Party or Parties unless such Party or Parties shall be
entitled to a refund in excess of three percent (3%) of the amount calculated by the Common Area
Manager as such Party or Parties’ Allocable Share for the applicable Fiscal Year, in which case
the Common Area Manager shall pay the reasonable cost of such audit. The Common Area
Manager shall retain the right to dispute the results of such audit for a period of sixty (60) days
following receipt of such audit, and the Common Area Manager’s election not to contest the results
of such audit during the sixty (60) day period shall be deemed acceptance of such audit. If any
dispute remains thirty (30) days after receipt by the Parties of the Common Area Manager’s
written notice of such dispute, then such dispute shall be deemed to be an Operational Dispute
which shall be resolved pursuant to Section 14.3.

  ARTICLE 8
  USE RESTRICTIONS

  8.1  Compliance with Applicable Laws and Project Entitlements and
Requirements. Each Party shall comply with, and such Parties shall use commercially
reasonable efforts to ensure that its Permitted Users comply with, all Applicable Laws, the Project
Entitlements, and the applicable Ground Leases relative to their use of the Plaza Improvements
Area. No illegal activities shall be conducted within the Plaza Improvements Area. The Plaza
Improvements Area shall be used and operated in accordance with the provisions of this
Declaration, the Project Entitlements, Applicable Laws.

  8.2  No Changes to Entitlements. No applications or requests for amending, revising
or otherwise changing the zoning, land use or other regulations affecting the Plaza Improvements
Area shall be made by any Party without the prior written approval of the Owners.

  8.3  Variances and Conditional Use Permits. No Owner shall submit an application
for a conditional use permit or variance for their respective portion of the Plaza Improvements
Area (“Conditional Use Permit”) unless such application is approved by all of the Owners in their
reasonable discretion prior to submittal to the applicable Governmental Agency. Each Owner
shall be responsible for all costs incurred in obtaining and satisfying requirements imposed under
a Conditional Use Permit for its portion of the Plaza Improvements Area. Any Owner obtaining a
Conditional Use Permit for its portion of the Plaza Improvements Area shall provide such
Conditional Use Permit to the other Owners and each of the Owners shall have the right to enforce
the terms of the Conditional Use Permit.

  8.4  Further Subdivisions. In no event may any Declarant further subdivide its Parcel
without the approval of all of the Owners.

   8.5  Occupants and Permitted Users. Each Party is responsible for the compliance
by its Lessees and Occupants, and each of their Permitted Users, with all the obligations and
restrictions in this Declaration, including, without limitation, the use restrictions set forth in this
Article 7.

  8.6  Insurance Requirements. The Parties shall not, without the prior written approval
of the Owners, do anything that would materially increase the premiums of any policy of insurance
maintained by any Declarant or other Owner or would render any portion of the Plaza
Improvements Area uninsurable, or create any valid defense to any Owner’s right to collect
Insurance Proceeds (as hereinafter defined), or cause any insurance policy to be cancelled, or
cause a refusal to renew the same.

  8.7  Hazardous Materials. No Party shall, and no Party shall allow any of its
Occupants and other Permitted Users to, release, generate, use, store, dump, transport, handle
or dispose of any Hazardous Materials within the City Property in violation of Applicable Laws or
otherwise permit the presence of any Hazardous Material on, under, or about the City Property in
violation of Applicable Laws. If Hazardous Materials are released within the City Property in
violation of any Applicable Laws and such release occurred as a direct or indirect result of a
Party’s or such Party’s Permitted Users’ use, handling, storage or transportation of such
Hazardous Materials, such Party shall be solely responsible and liable for the prompt cleanup and
remediation of any resulting contamination and will indemnify, protect, defend and hold the other
Parties harmless from any and all Claims suffered by or incurred by such parties.

  8.8  Refuse Removal. All waste, recycling, packing materials, debris and other refuse
(except for Hazardous Materials, which shall be governed by the provision of Section 7.7) shall
promptly be removed from the Plaza Improvements Area, in compliance with all Governmental
Requirements.

  8.9  Emissions. No use shall be permitted on or within any portion of the City Property
which: (a) emits unreasonable amounts of dust, debris, dirt, cinders, fumes, odors, radiation,
gases, or vapors; (b) discharges contaminated liquid or solid wastes or other toxic, noxious or
harmful matter into the atmosphere or any Utility Facilities of the Master Project or the Affordable
Housing Project, which may adversely affect (i) the health or safety of persons or (ii) the use or
enjoyment of the Master Project and/or the Affordable Housing Project or any part thereof; or
(c) causes obstructions to the Project Drainage Facilities. The foregoing shall not include
emissions resulting from work permitted to be performed hereunder so long as appropriate
construction practices are adhered to and so long as the Person performing the work conforms
to the requirements of this Declaration.

  8.10 Non-Smoking. The Master Project and the Affordable Housing Project are non-
smoking projects and no smoking shall be permitted in any Project Exterior Areas or any portion
of the Plaza Improvements Area.

  8.11 Oil and Mineral Rights. No oil drilling, oil development operations, oil refining,
quarrying, or mining operations of any kind shall be permitted upon or in any portion of the City
Property nor, subsequent to the recording of this Declaration, shall oil wells, tanks, tunnels, or
mineral excavations or shafts be installed upon the surface of any portion of the City Property or
within five hundred feet (500’) below the surface of such portion of the City Property. No derrick
or other structure designed for use in boring for water, oil or natural gas shall be erected,
maintained or permitted upon any portion of the City Property.

  ARTICLE 17
  GENERAL PROVISIONS

  17.1 Headings. The headings used in this Declaration are for convenience only and
are not to be used to interpret the meaning of any of the provisions of this Declaration.

  17.2 Severability. The provisions of this Declaration shall be deemed independent and
severable, and the invalidity or partial invalidity or unenforceability of any provision or provisions
of it shall not invalidate any other provisions. In the event that any phrase, clause, sentence,
paragraph, section, article or other portion of this Declaration shall be or become illegal, null, void,
against public policy, or otherwise unenforceable, for any reason, the remaining portions of this
Declaration shall not be affected thereby and shall remain in force and effect to the fullest extent
permissible by Applicable Laws.

  17.3 Cumulative Remedies; No Waiver. Each remedy provided for in this Declaration
shall be cumulative and not exclusive. Failure to exercise any remedy provided for in this
Declaration shall not, under any circumstances, be construed as a waiver.

  17.4 Adjustments for Inflation. Any dollar amounts specified in this Declaration shall
be increased proportionately every five (5) years after the recordation of this Declaration by the
increase in the CPI to adjust for any changes in the value of the dollar after the effective date of
this Declaration.

  17.5 Liberal Construction. The provisions of this Declaration shall be liberally
construed to effectuate its purpose so that the Plaza Improvements Area and other portions of
the Master Project and Affordable Housing Project shall operate as a mixed-use commercial and
residential development.

  17.6 Notice. All notices required by this Declaration shall be in writing and either
(a) personally served at the appropriate address (including by means of professional messenger
service or recognized overnight delivery service, provided that any such delivery is confirmed by
written receipts signed on behalf of the receiving Party or by adequate proof of service),
(b) deposited in the United States mail, postage prepaid, certified or registered mail, return receipt
requested, or (c) nationally recognized overnight courier, addressed to the appropriate addressee,
and shall be deemed received and effective upon actual receipt or refusal of delivery.

  17.7 Joint and Several Liability. If a Party consists of more than one (1) Person, each
such Person shall be jointly and severally liable for payment of Assessments, and performance
of all obligations (including, without limitation, indemnification obligations) arising under any
provision of this Declaration.
